Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 27 May 2003 01:27:15 +0200, "Kulaid"
<kulaid.ne...@web2news.net> wrote:

>Damage-dealing strikes Harry makes against non-mortal allies are at +1
>damage.

In other words, Harry has 1 strength against all opponents who are not
non-mortal allies. He has 2 strength against Garous, and War Ghouls,
and Wraiths and such.

>err, does this only apply to allies?

Absolutely, the card text is clear.

> or anybody that's not a mortal ally?

Any ally that isn't mortal, right.

> Vampires included?

Vampires are not non-mortal allies, so Harry has 1 strength against
them.

Carpe noctem.

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>>Damage-dealing strikes Harry makes against non-mortal allies are at +1
>>damage.
>
>In other words, Harry has 1 strength against all opponents who are not
>non-mortal allies. He has 2 strength against Garous, and War Ghouls,
>and Wraiths and such.
>

Well, it's more than that (simply a strength bonus), isn't it? If Harry is
using hand strikes then yes, he effectively has 2 strength against Garous, but
his special also applies to non-strength strikes (similar to Reverend
Blackwood's ability). Thus he Body Flares for 3R aggravated vs. Garous for
instance.

Halcyan 2

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <hi95dvsnfodmgukt0...@4ax.com>, The Lasombra

<TheLa...@hotmail.com> writes:
>> Vampires included?
>
>Vampires are not non-mortal allies, so Harry has 1 strength against
>them.

I believe the confusion is between:

(non-mortal) allies
and:
non-(mortal allies)

Vampires would fit under the second one - not being a "mortal ally".

The first one is right, of course. The hyphen aids reading.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Yeah. I remember all the confusion Judgment: Camarilla Segregation gave about
people trying to burn other player's pool for controlling allies.

Or giving Cornelius +1 bleed when bleeding a Renegade Garou's controller.

Of having IC members use Protect Thine Own to burn Muddles.

Oh, wait, that's right. There's no confusion there.
The hyphen doesn't allow any other reading.

If you know what "non-Camarilla vampire" means, you should know what
"non-mortal ally" means.
